articles.title: 'Tis the season: NCR's most polluted fortnight begins
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The worst of Delhi's pollution season may be here.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The worst of Delhi's pollution season may be here. The capital has entered the fortnight that usually records the year's highest AQI levels, coinciding with a peak in farm fires, increased traffic around festivals, additional emissions from firecrackers and unfavourable meteorological conditions that trap pollutants.An analysis by TOI of CPCB data from 2015 till now revealed that Nov 1-15 is the capital's most polluted period in a year, with a high number of severe days and average AQI of 374.This year, Diwali will be celebrated on Nov 8 and the share of stubble burning in Delhi’s air quality is expected to rise significantly in the coming days. Ahead of the wedding season and festivals, the city also witnesses an increase in traffic congestion. Firecrackers, moreover, add to the existing pollution load.Anumita Roychowdhury, executive director-research and advocacy, Centre for Science and Environment, said Delhi has once again entered its most difficult winter phase, where plummeting temperatures, calm winds, and atmospheric inversion trap toxic emissions close to the surface.“As seasonal farm and waste fires combine with local traffic emissions, industrial combustion, and festive firecrackers, the airshed becomes a hotspot. Yet forecasting trends in gross pollution and source emissions remains challenging. It is, therefore, necessary to track more diligently real-time action and emission changes on the ground in Delhi and across NCR,” said Roychowdhury.Last year, this period was relatively better due to an early Diwali and the low impact of stubble burning. It still saw three severe days, with an AQI above 400 on a scale of 500. In 2024, Delhi saw eight ‘severe’ days in Nov, and of these, two were recorded in the first half of the month. In 2023, the city recorded six severe days in the Nov 1-15 period.The second most polluted fortnight in a year, analysis of CPCB data showed, is Dec 16-31, with average AQI of 346. This fortnight witnesses low temperatures and dense fog which traps pollutants. It also records increased traffic and use of firecrackers due to wedding season, Christmas and New Year’s Eve. Last year, this period saw five severe days, including a severe-plus day when AQI touched 461.The third most polluted spell is typically Jan 1-15 when unfavourable meteorological conditions, including dense fog, low temperatures and calm winds, continue. From 2016 to 2026, average AQI for Jan 1-15 was 329.3.CPCB has been calculating the AQI since April 2015.The Nov 16-30 period is close behind, with average AQI of 329, followed by Oct 16-31 when winter starts setting in, with average AQI of 281.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Idle engines, rising emissions: Traffic tailbacks add to Delhi's pollution woes
articles.summary: Barricades and checkpoints could become a regular sight as Delhi bars non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside the city.
articles.body: Barricades and checkpoints could become a regular sight as Delhi bars non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside the city. While most borders saw little congestion Sunday, Gurgaon and Ghazipur saw tailbacks. TOI’s Ishita Jairath crunches ground estimates to calculate the fuel consumed and CO2 emissions generated by vehicles idling in these queues. The big question: How much CO2 is being released by vehicles waiting with their engines running?Air pollution calculationsAverage co₂ emissions per vehicle: approximately 30.7 grams per minute of idling.Waiting time varies depending on where vehicles are positioned in the tailback. While some commuters may get through within 10 minutes, those further back could remain stuck for 15–20 minutes.Gurgaon borderEstimated tailback: 400 carsApprox co₂ emissions per minute: 12.3 kgIf vehicles idle for:10 minutes: around 123 kg (0.123 metric tonnes) of co₂.15 minutes: around 184 kg (0.184 metric tonnes) of co₂.20 minutes: around 245 kg (0.245 metric tonnes) of co₂.Ghazipur borderEstimated tailback: 30–40 vehiclesApprox co₂ emissions per minute: 0.9–1.2 kgIf vehicles idle for:10 minutes: 9–12 kg of co₂.15 minutes: 14–18 kg.20 minutes: 18–25 kg.Air pollution calculationThe us energy information administration states that burning one us gallon of gasoline produces approximately 8,887 grams of co₂. Since one us gallon is approximately 3.785 litres, this translates to around 2.35 kg of co₂ per litre of petrol burned.Emissions assumed: burning one litre of petrol releases approximately 2.3 kg of co₂.Calculation methodologyFuel consumed per minute = number of vehicles × 0.8 litres ÷ 60.Co₂ emissions per minute = fuel consumed × 2.3 kg.Emissions over the waiting period = per-minute emissions × number of minutes.Note: these estimates are based on available data, ground assessments and general assumptions. Actual figures may vary depending on vehicle models, engine capacity, fuel type, maintenance, idling conditions and time spent in queues. The estimates represent a hypothetical continuous-idling scenario.AssumptionsAll vehicle engines were assumed to be running.All vehicles were assumed to be petrol cars.Each car was assumed to consume 0.8 litres of petrol per hour while idling, equivalent to approximately 13.3 ml per minute.Vehicles were assumed to be stationary and continuously idling during the calculated waiting period.Waiting periods of 10, 15 and 20 minutes were used for illustrative calculations, as actual waiting times varied depending on the vehicle's position in the tailback.Expert opinions“Tailpipes dump toxic gas straight into our lungs at street level, and while clean vehicles help stop that poison, they continue to resuspend fine road dust into the air. Cleaning our air takes more than changing vehicle technology. It demands dust-free roads in our cities and unified action across state borders. Air has no boundaries, and northern india cannot solve a regional health crisis with isolated city-level band-aids.”— Shreya GadepalliMobility expert“A seamless transition requires automated enforcement, well-equipped peripheral holding areas, synchronised inter-state logistics, real-time tracking, and clear phase-in support for operators.”— Anumita RoychowdhuryExecutive director-research and advocacy, centre for science and environmentYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: US explores route to bring Russian gas back to Europe through Ukraine: Report
articles.summary: The US is exploring a plan to bring Russian natural gas back into the European market through pipelines crossing Ukraine, in a bid to secure an energy
articles.body: The US is exploring a plan to bring Russian natural gas back into the European market through pipelines crossing Ukraine, in a bid to secure an energy truce between Moscow and Kyiv before winter. The proposal is part of wider efforts to advance peace negotiations, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing officials from the US, Europe and Ukraine.The arrangement could see a US intermediary handle the sale of Russian gas, potentially bypassing European sanctions while giving American investors a stake in the business. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff raised the proposal during their visits to Moscow and Kyiv in September, people familiar with the discussions told the WSJ.The idea faces a major obstacle: Europe's stated policy of ending its reliance on Russian energy. EU legislation requires member states to phase out all Russian natural gas purchases by the end of 2027. Several European leaders have also ruled out returning to dependence on supplies from a country they consider a major security threat.Yet Washington believes the prospect of reopening a lucrative European market could persuade Russian President Vladimir Putin to agree to an energy ceasefire. The proposed route would use the Soviet-era pipeline system connecting Siberia's Urengoi gas fields to Europe through Ukraine. Kyiv, in turn, could earn much-needed money from transit charges.The proposal had lost momentum last month after Ukraine halted attacks on Russian refineries following pressure from US President Donald Trump. The pause lasted nearly two weeks, even as Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure continued and Moscow began sending diesel to the US. Washington subsequently turned its attention to the possibility of negotiating a wider peace settlement.That pause is now over. Ukraine launched attacks on three major Russian refineries over three days, beginning Friday, bringing the question of an energy truce back into focus. The renewed urgency comes ahead of planned three-way talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi in mid-November. Moscow has so far resisted US efforts to secure such an arrangement, according to the WSJ.A possible financial incentive for MoscowThe White House has also discussed safeguards to prevent Russia from using gas revenues to bankroll its military campaign. Under one proposal, proceeds from European sales would be placed in an escrow account in a third-party jurisdiction, a senior US official told the WSJ.American negotiators have presented the arrangement to European governments as a way to ease energy costs at a time when the continent is preparing for winter with relatively low gas reserves. They believe access to the European market could give Putin a strong financial reason to accept a deal.The proposal would represent a dramatic shift in Trump's approach to Russian energy. During his first term, he repeatedly criticised then-German Chancellor Angela Merkel for backing the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, warning that the project would leave Germany “captive to Russia”. His administration imposed sanctions on the pipeline in late 2019.Russia's subsequent invasion of Ukraine reinforced European concerns about the risks of relying on Moscow for energy. Before the war, Russian gas accounted for 45% of Europe's supplies. That share has since fallen to 11%, with US liquefied natural gas now making up 30% of European consumption.The EU has since moved to dismantle its dependence on Russian gas, with a complete phase-out mandated by the end of 2027. Its stated position is that purchases should not resume even after a comprehensive peace agreement, much less under a temporary ceasefire that leaves Russia's war effort intact.EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen reiterated that position in an October interview with a Hungarian newspaper, which his office confirmed.“I certainly would not trust Russia. Even if there were peace tomorrow, which we all hope for,” he said.Europe's resistance faces a new energy testDespite the public opposition, the Trump administration believes economic pressures could make European governments reconsider. Some senior officials, however, have privately rejected the idea in strong terms.A senior Nordic official said buying Russian gas again would contradict everything Europe stands for. Another senior official from a large European country likened the proposal to former British leader Neville Chamberlain sacrificing Czechoslovakia to Hitler in exchange for business deals, the WSJ reported.Washington is also considering the possibility of restoring gas supplies through Nord Stream as part of a broader settlement. The US sees such an arrangement as potentially helping not only to end the Ukraine war but also to ease longstanding tensions between Moscow and America's European allies.A senior US official told the WSJ that Merkel's mistake had been to pursue the pipeline without first securing a broader security arrangement with Russia that Moscow could accept.The Nord Stream route, however, would be difficult to revive. Nord Stream 1 stopped deliveries in August 2022, while Nord Stream 2 never entered service. Both pipelines were badly damaged in underwater explosions in September 2022, which were attributed to Ukraine. Their restoration would require considerable time and the resolution of major political and regulatory obstacles.The route through Ukraine, on the other hand, offers a quicker alternative. The pipeline network connects to Slovakia and extends towards Austria and Germany. It could be brought back into operation almost immediately, as limited gas flows continued through it until January 2025, despite the ongoing war.US officials have also discussed other economic arrangements during negotiations. One proposal that could significantly lower gas prices across Europe has drawn interest from European leaders, a US official said. However, any such arrangement would be tied to a comprehensive peace deal.The energy situation could further complicate Europe's position. The conflict involving Iran has disrupted Qatari LNG shipments, leaving cargoes stranded inside the Persian Gulf. Energy prices have climbed globally despite an increase in oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.According to the EU, the conflict has added 100 billion euros, or around $112 billion, to Europe's energy costs. Meanwhile, underground gas storage across the continent is about 75% full, leaving Europe on course to enter winter with reserves below the nine-year average, EU energy regulators said.The prospect of cheaper Russian supplies has also become a political issue in Germany. The far-right Alternative for Germany has made restoring imports of low-cost Russian gas a central plank of its campaign ahead of the 2028 national elections.For Ukraine, the calculation could be different if renewed gas transit forms part of an agreement that protects its energy infrastructure. Diplomats told the WSJ that Kyiv's backing could make it easier for European governments to reconsider the proposal, particularly if a ceasefire prevents blackouts and a humanitarian crisis in major Ukrainian cities.A collapse of energy supplies could trigger another wave of refugees in the coming months. The risk is compounded by Ukraine's dwindling air-defence capabilities, with the US restricting supplies of Patriot interceptors amid a global shortage linked to the war on Iran.You use AI every day. articles.title: Brandon Castaneda and his mother turned a family cooking idea into EZ Bombs; in 2026, the seasoning startup raised $25 million after expanding to more than 8,000 stores
articles.summary: Brandon Castaneda, his mother Tina Castaneda and sister Nichole Munoz turned a family cooking tradition into EZ Bombs, a food business selling
articles.body: Brandon Castaneda, his mother Tina Castaneda and sister Nichole Munoz turned a family cooking tradition into EZ Bombs, a food business selling shelf-stable seasoning products for traditional Mexican dishes. Founded in late 2023, the company has grown from selling through TikTok Shop and Amazon to securing distribution across more than 8,000 US retail locations, including Walmart, Target and Costco. On 14 October 2026, EZ Bombs announced a $25 million Series A funding round led by CAVU Consumer Partners. The investment will support its retail expansion, manufacturing capacity, new product development and executive recruitment.What inspired Brandon Castaneda and his mother to launch EZ BombsAccording to the company's official announcement published in Business Wire, EZ Bombs was founded by Brandon Castaneda's desire to recreate the meals his mother prepared while he was growing up. Although he enjoyed Tina Castaneda's cooking, he found it difficult to prepare the same dishes himself.This inspired Brandon and Tina to explore a way of packaging the flavour bases behind her recipes into convenient, shelf-stable products. His sister, Nichole Munoz, subsequently joined the venture, bringing her experience of building social media audiences to lead the company's social media strategy. Tina became the face of the brand, while Brandon took on the role of chief executive officer.The family founded EZ Bombs in late 2023, building its business around a simple concept: making traditionally time-consuming meals easier to prepare without requiring home cooks to source and measure numerous individual ingredients.Why did EZ Bombs introduce the Birria Bomb as its first productEZ Bombs introduced its first product, the Birria Bomb, to simplify the preparation of birria, a traditional Mexican dish known for its slow-cooked meat and chile-rich broth.Preparing birria traditionally involves combining ingredients such as dried chillies, garlic, onions, tomatoes and spices to create its distinctive flavour base. EZ Bombs brought these ingredients together in a single, pre-portioned seasoning ball.The product can be added directly to a slow cooker, pressure cooker or cooking pot, allowing consumers to prepare the dish without separately measuring and preparing each seasoning and aromatic ingredient.The company also pointed to the increasing popularity of birria in the United States. According to Datassential, birria's presence on US restaurant menus increased by 350 per cent between 2021 and 2026. EZ Bombs used the dish as the starting point for its seasoning bomb concept before extending the product range to other recipes.EZ Bombs sell more than one million units through TikTok ShopTikTok Shop became EZ Bombs' first major sales channel, allowing the company to demonstrate how its products worked through short videos and live shopping sessions.Tina Castaneda featured in videos showing herself dropping a Birria Bomb into a cooking pot. The demonstration illustrated how the product could replace the preparation of more than a dozen individual ingredients, making the cooking process more convenient.EZ Bombs became the number one food and beverage product on TikTok Shop in 2025. It sold more than one million units and recorded the platform's largest live-show sales.The company's social media presence helped it introduce the product to consumers before expanding into traditional retail distribution. Its marketing also remained closely connected to Tina's original recipes, which continued to provide the foundation for its seasoning bombs.Which major US retailers sell EZ Bombs seasoning productsAfter establishing its presence through online marketplaces, EZ Bombs moved into physical retail distribution. The company reported that it had expanded from zero retail locations at the beginning of 2025 to more than 8,000 locations by October 2026.Its products are now available through major US retailers, including Walmart, Target, Costco, Kroger, Albertsons and Publix. Consumers can also purchase them through Amazon, TikTok Shop and the company's official website.Beyond its original Birria Bomb, EZ Bombs has introduced separate seasoning bombs for Pozole, Tinga, Chicken Chipotle and Chile Colorado.Each product contains the flavour base for a particular dish, eliminating the need for home cooks to identify, measure and prepare the individual ingredients themselves. The company said additional Mexican seasoning bombs were scheduled to enter retail stores later in 2026.EZ Bombs uses its $25 million funding to expand its seasoning businessOn October 14, 2026, EZ Bombs announced a $25 million Series A funding round led by CAVU Consumer Partners. The investment comes as the company builds on its growth across social commerce platforms, online marketplaces and national retail distribution.As part of the agreement, CAVU Principal Brandon Neumann will join EZ Bombs' board of directors. The funding will be directed towards expanding retail distribution, increasing manufacturing capacity, developing new products and recruiting additional executives.Neumann highlighted the company's approach to simplifying meal preparation as one of the factors behind the investment. "Most seasonings are sold as ingredients while EZ Bombs starts with the meal," he said.He also pointed to the company's transition from online demand to national retail distribution, noting that its growth and profitability from the beginning had attracted CAVU's attention.The investment will also bring support from UNCOMMON, CAVU's in-house value-add team. The team will work with EZ Bombs on retail expansion, brand development, digital commerce and executive team development as the business grows.Campany expansion plans following its $25 million Series A fundingEZ Bombs plans to build on its existing product range, which includes seasoning bombs for Birria, Pozole, Tinga, Chicken Chipotle and Chile Colorado. Additional Mexican seasoning products are expected to enter retail stores later in 2026.The company also intends to increase its manufacturing capacity to support its expanding distribution network. Executive recruitment is another priority identified in its funding announcement. EZ Bombs said it was hiring across the United States, including for remote positions.Founded by Brandon Castaneda, Tina Castaneda and Nichole Munoz in late 2023, EZ Bombs has grown from a family-led online business into a food brand available in more than 8,000 retail locations. Its $25 million Series A investment from CAVU Consumer Partners marks a new stage in its expansion as it looks to introduce more convenient seasoning products to US households.You use AI every day. articles.title: Netanyahu pushing Donald Trump for nuclear strike on Iran? US commentator makes big claim
articles.summary: US media personality and political commentator Tucker Carlson has claimed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing US President Donald
articles.body: US media personality and political commentator Tucker Carlson has claimed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing US President Donald Trump to launch a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Washington could take a decision on the use of nuclear weapons within days.In a detailed post on X on Monday, Carlson claimed that the proposed target could be Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Tehran has restarted its nuclear enrichment programme.He argued that conventional US weapons would not be able to penetrate the mountain's granite to reach underground tunnels where enrichment activity is supposedly taking place."Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran," Carlson wrote.He further claimed that Netanyahu had been pushing for such an operation and quoted an unnamed source as saying, "Bibi calls Trump about it every day."Carlson's post did not provide independently verifiable evidence for the claims about a possible nuclear strike or the alleged pressure being exerted by Netanyahu.Carlson claims Netanyahu wants war to continueCarlson linked the alleged push for military action to Netanyahu's political position following last week's elections in Israel. He claimed the Israeli prime minister would struggle to form a government without Trump's direct intervention and could face investigations and possible jail if he lost office."Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war," Carlson wrote.He also alleged that several senior US officials were backing Netanyahu's position and opposed a negotiated settlement with Iran.Carlson named US defence secretary Pete Hegseth and Centcom commander Brad Cooper, while also claiming that secretary of state Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe were following the Israeli prime minister's lead.Carlson further claimed that former US president Barack Obama had opposed the Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha during a recent meeting. He did not provide details or evidence to substantiate that assertion either.The commentator also said that Netanyahu had travelled secretly to Abu Dhabi on September 27 to seek the United Arab Emirates' support for a final military operation against Iran, but that the Emiratis had refused.Warning over regional and global consequencesCarlson warned that another escalation could have serious consequences for the Gulf region and the global economy, pointing to damage to oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and disruptions to energy and fertiliser markets.He claimed that 11 of the approximately 850 supertankers used to transport oil globally had been badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October.On the consequences of a possible nuclear strike, Carlson alleged that a ground explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Persian Gulf and affect the water supply of 100 million people. He also warned that the use of a nuclear weapon by the US could set a precedent for other countries.Carlson claimed that Russia had told at least two governments that a US nuclear strike on Iran would give it the freedom to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. He also cited possible nuclear escalation involving North Korea and South Korea.He further alleged that the US administration had quietly revised its nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier.Trump weighing diplomacy as Iran talks continueCarlson's claims come amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to resume negotiations between Washington and Tehran, even as the possibility of renewed military action remains under discussion.US President Donald Trump and Netanyahu spoke by phone on Saturday about the state of negotiations with Iran and the possibility of returning to military operations, according to an Axios report.The report said Netanyahu was pressing Trump to launch fresh strikes after Tuesday's US midterm elections, while the US president wanted to allow negotiations to continue. An Israeli source described the conversation as "tough", while a US source called it "direct".Trump later described the conversation as a "very good talk" and confirmed that Iran was among the subjects discussed, without providing further details.Trump has said negotiations with Iran were "going fine" and that he was not "in much of a hurry". However, he also indicated that the US still needed to address one or two Iranian nuclear sites, specifically referring to Pickaxe Mountain."We can do that in 10 minutes. We have that planned. You can look at Pickaxe Mountain. We need to take care of that. We can do that very quickly," Trump said.Meanwhile, US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter last week to Iran's national security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, regarding the possibility of restarting negotiations.Qatari mediators also held discussions with Iranian officials for a third consecutive day on Sunday in an effort to facilitate an agreement to resume direct talks between Washington and Tehran.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said no agreement had been reached and that progress depended on the US responding to Tehran's questions."We are making every effort in this regard and hope that the other side will demonstrate enough rationality to choose diplomacy over other paths," Araghchi said.Carlson, meanwhile, claimed that Trump was listening to Vance and US envoy Steve Witkoff, who he said believed a deal with Iran could still be reached.He urged the US administration to pursue diplomacy, warning against a nuclear escalation.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Nuclear war rehearsal': North Korea vows to strengthen deterrent after US-South Korea drills
articles.summary: North Korea has vowed to speed up efforts to strengthen its nuclear deterrent, accusing the US and South Korea of conducting a joint military exercise
articles.body: North Korea has vowed to speed up efforts to strengthen its nuclear deterrent, accusing the US and South Korea of conducting a joint military exercise that amounted to a “nuclear war rehearsal” against Pyongyang, state media KCNA reported on Monday.Kim Jong Sik, a deputy department director in the ruling Workers’ Party, said the Iron Mace exercise demonstrated that Washington remained committed to its “wild ambition to stifle North Korea with nukes”. He added that such threats were “escalating with each passing day”.The US and South Korea conducted the Iron Mace exercise from September 29 to October 2. The drills were aimed at integrating US nuclear capabilities with South Korea’s conventional forces, according to Seoul’s military, according to Reuters.Kim said the exercise, along with other joint military activities by the two allies, highlighted the need for North Korea to strengthen its nuclear forces at a faster pace.Analysts said it was unusual for Kim, a senior official involved in North Korea’s nuclear and missile development, to issue a statement outlining the country’s nuclear policy. Such statements are more commonly made by the defence or foreign ministry.Tensions between the two Koreas have also risen following a border mine explosion in September. North Korea later threatened to resume loudspeaker propaganda broadcasts towards the South by the end of October. South Korea’s military said on Monday there were no confirmed indications that Pyongyang had carried out the threat.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: '2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of the approximately three lakh shops in markets surrounding the rally venue remained shut amid concerns over traffic restrictions, congestion and the expected arrival of large crowds.The disruption also affected the movement of customers, suppliers and dealers from towns surrounding the national capital. According to Goyal, around three lakh to four lakh people who regularly travel to Delhi for business did not arrive, while approximately 5,000 vehicles, including tempos and trucks, could not transport goods to markets in Old Delhi and Central Delhi.“Due to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups—comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)—about 80% of these shops—roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000—remained closed today,” he said.Goyal added that loading and unloading operations were disrupted, affecting wholesale and retail businesses during one of the busiest periods of the year.“The movement of goods—loading and unloading—was completely disrupted. During the peak Diwali season, these markets with individual turnovers collectively generate business worth approximately 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees. Even where shops remained open, sales were virtually non-existent; there were simply no customers,” he said.Putting the estimated losses at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, Goyal questioned who would compensate traders for the business disruption.“The question now arises: who will compensate for this loss, or who will make up for it—will the organisers do so?” he said.He said the timing of the rally had compounded the impact, as traders were preparing for the festive rush ahead of Dhanteras, scheduled four days later. Businesses in the affected markets depend heavily on the movement of customers and goods during this period.Traders had warned of business losses ahead of rallyAhead of the gathering, traders across several major commercial hubs in Delhi had opposed holding the rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season. They warned that traffic congestion and restrictions could disrupt wholesale markets and affect the livelihoods of thousands of daily-wage workers.The Automotive Parts Merchant Association (APMA), based at Kashmere Gate, said the rally's location could affect commercial activity across a three-kilometre radius, covering several major trading hubs in the capital.APMA president Vinay Narang said traders were not opposed to democratic protests but objected to the timing and choice of venue."We are not aligned with any political party, nor are we against democratic protests. But the timing and the venue are completely wrong. Ramlila Maidan is located in the middle of Asia’s largest commercial zone—with major markets like Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Daryaganj, Mori Gate, and Kashmere Gate within a three-kilometre radius," Narang said.Rahul's video appeal for participants to shop from local tradersAmid concerns raised by traders' associations, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from their stores during the festive season.In a video message posted on X on Saturday, Gandhi urged participants to combine their participation in the protest with shopping from small businesses.“Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,” Gandhi said.“Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” he added.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha also accused the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's potential economic impact.“I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours,” he said, adding, “But let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders.”INDIA bloc holds rally against SIR, alleged electoral irregularitiesThe INDIA bloc held the rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging irregularities in the exercise.Several Opposition leaders attended the gathering, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Protesters also raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod", demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Apple HomeView's built-in camera may gain recording and motion detection features
articles.summary: Apple’s new HomeView smart display may be able to act as a home security camera, according to references found in its software, The Verge reports.
articles.body: Apple’s new HomeView smart display may be able to act as a home security camera, according to references found in its software, The Verge reports. A Reddit user spotted the feature in the settings files of HomeView Software 27.2. Apple has not announced anything about it, and Digital Trends notes that the feature is not active in the current software.The HomeView is Apple’s recently unveiled smart home display. It already has a built-in camera for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. The camera is a 12MP unit that can recognise people on sight, which matters in a home shared by a whole family. The settings files suggest Apple could also use the same hardware for motion detection, live streaming and video recording through HomeKit Secure Video.Hidden code points to security camera modeAccording to a report by The Verge, Reddit user "pdfu" uncovered references within HomeView software version 27.2 that describe a dedicated security camera mode. The code strings mention motion detection, live streaming, video recording options, and several privacy-focused features. One setup screen reportedly states: "Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video." The discovery suggests that Apple may be planning to leverage the HomeView's built-in camera for home monitoring purposes, although the company has not officially announced such a feature.HomeView already includes a built-in cameraApple unveiled the HomeView smart display at its "Welcome Home" event in October 2026. The device features a 7-inch display and a 12-megapixel camera designed for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. The camera can recognise multiple users and personalise content based on who is standing in front of the device. The HomeView currently serves as a central smart home control hub, allowing users to manage connected devices, view feeds from security cameras and access Siri-powered smart home features.Privacy-focused features reportedly in developmentThe leaked code strings indicate that Apple is building several privacy protections into the potential security camera mode. According to the report, video feeds would only be viewable by members of the household, while the device would display a visual indicator and play a sound whenever someone starts watching the camera feed or when recording begins. Household members would also reportedly receive notifications whenever security camera settings are changed. The software code further points to configurable settings that would allow users to determine what the camera should detect, stream or record depending on whether they are at home, away or asleep.Apple yet to confirm featureWhile the code references strongly hint at upcoming functionality, Apple has not publicly confirmed plans to turn HomeView into a security camera. The Verge noted that the company may still be refining privacy safeguards before rolling out such a feature, given Apple's longstanding emphasis on user privacy and security. If introduced, the feature would further expand HomeView's role within Apple's growing smart home ecosystem and could make the device a more direct competitor to smart displays from rivals that already offer integrated home monitoring capabilities.You use AI every day. articles.body: LUCKNOW: A 52-year-old man allegedly murdered his wife by gouging out her right eye with a knife and then crushing her face and head with a brick before dying by suicide at their home in Hardoi district's Pali area late Saturday, police said.The incident came to light when the couple's children returned from a local fair and found both parents dead in separate rooms.The deceased were identified as Lalput Rathore and his wife, Janki (50). The incident took place around 11:30pm. Preliminary investigation suggests the couple had an argument linked to a long-standing domestic dispute.Police suspect Lalput, who allegedly doubted his wife's character, attacked her with a knife, inflicting fatal injuries on her abdomen. He then allegedly struck her head and face with a brick, killing her on the spot.After the attack, Lalput went to another room and hanged himself, police said.The crime came to light when the couple's eight-year-old son, Pushpendra, returned from the fair and found his mother lying in a pool of blood. Family members then searched for Lalput and found his body hanging from a noose in another room. The children's cries drew neighbours, who rushed to the house and alerted police.Police recovered a blood-stained knife and a brick, believed to have been used in the killing. Both bodies were sent for post-mortem examination.Neighbours told police that Lalput frequently quarrelled with Janki and allegedly assaulted her, particularly after consuming alcohol. A local resident also claimed that frequent visitors to the house, purportedly linked to Lalput's alleged involvement in illicit liquor sales, often fuelled his suspicions and triggered arguments.The couple had eight children, including six sons and two daughters. articles.title: A Kentucky man married his partner of nearly 30 years in a hospital 15 days before she died; after her daughter challenged the ceremony, an October 30 appeals court overturned the ruling that had voided the marriage
articles.summary: A Kentucky man who married his long-time partner in a hospital room just 15 days before her death won an appeal on Friday in a dispute over whether their
articles.body: A Kentucky man who married his long-time partner in a hospital room just 15 days before her death won an appeal on Friday in a dispute over whether their marriage was legally valid.Victor Allen Wilson and Betty Sue Conkright had been together for nearly 30 years before marrying on August 24, 2023. After Conkright died, her daughter challenged the marriage, questioning both her mother's ability to consent and the way the marriage license was obtained. On Friday, the Kentucky Court of Appeals overturned an earlier ruling that had invalidated the marriage and sent the case back for further examination.Conkright was admitted to a hospital in Lexington, Kentucky, in August 2023, according to the information available in the ruling. She was suffering from serious liver-related complications, and her condition had affected her ability to think and communicate clearly. That same day, her daughter Tonya Hart sought legal authority to make decisions for her and was appointed temporary emergency guardian.There were already disagreements within the family. Hart, Wilson, and another of Conkright's daughters, Barbara Davis, were involved in a dispute over her care and access to her. A court subsequently restricted Wilson's and Davis's hospital visits to a few hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays, while Hart retained responsibility for medical decisions.Despite these circumstances, Wilson decided to marry Conkright. The couple had been romantically involved for approximately three decades and had lived together at different times. When later asked why they had never married, Wilson told the court that Conkright had been concerned about losing federal benefits.The unusual wedding Wilson obtained a marriage licence from the Bourbon County Clerk's Office on August 18, using Conkright's identification. She did not accompany him because she remained in hospital.By August 23, her health had deteriorated further and she had been transferred to intensive care. The following day, Wilson went to the hospital with Davis, Conkright's grandson and Reverend Douglass Hess, accompanied by his wife Brenda.Hess conducted the wedding in Conkright's room, with Davis and Brenda serving as witnesses. The ceremony was brief, lasting only a few minutes. Wilson submitted the completed marriage certificate to the clerk's office four days later. Conkright died on September 8.However, her death did not end the disagreement. Hart, who became administrator of her mother's estate, went to court to challenge the marriage. She argued that Conkright had not been capable of giving informed consent and raised concerns about pressure surrounding the wedding.Was Conkright conscious?The court heard different accounts of Conkright's condition. Hart described her mother as confused during her hospital stay. She said Conkright sometimes struggled to recognise people, had difficulty communicating and did not always know where she was. Although there were occasions when she appeared more alert, Hart maintained that the confusion continued.Conkright's son Robert supported those concerns. He told the court that his mother sometimes failed to recognise him, including on the day of the wedding. Neither he nor Hart had attended the ceremony, although both were at the hospital that day.The people who witnessed the wedding gave a different account. Reverend Hess said he had known the couple for about 25 years. Before agreeing to conduct the ceremony, he had told Wilson that he would not proceed if Conkright was unresponsive.According to Hess, she recognised him and indicated that she wanted to marry Wilson. His wife also testified about the short ceremony, which ended with Conkright appearing tired.Davis and Conkright's grandson similarly believed she was alert and recognised them. Wilson acknowledged that her awareness varied during her hospital stay but said she understood what was happening when they married.Why court declared marriage invalidApart from the disagreement over Conkright's condition, there was a problem with the marriage licence itself. Kentucky law requires both applicants to appear before the county clerk with identification. Wilson had obtained the licence alone, and the Bourbon County Clerk acknowledged that her office should not have issued it in those circumstances.Hess also testified that he had not known about Conkright's emergency guardianship or the problem with the licence. Had he known, he said, he would not have conducted the wedding.In July 2025, the Montgomery Circuit Court ruled that the marriage was invalid because the licence had been issued improperly. It did not make a separate finding on whether Conkright could consent or whether she had been subjected to coercion.Why appeals court overturned rulingThe appeals court disagreed with the lower court's approach. It said the mistake made by the clerk could not, by itself, justify invalidating the marriage after Conkright's death.The judges pointed out that Wilson had obtained a licence, a wedding ceremony had taken place and the marriage certificate had been officially recorded.However, they also found that Hart, acting for her mother's estate, was entitled to pursue the allegations concerning Conkright's mental capacity and possible coercion.The case will now return to the lower court, which must examine those questions before deciding whether the marriage should be invalidated. One appeals court judge dissented, arguing that the existing evidence was enough to uphold the earlier decision.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

Neither of their constituencies figured in the list.The two leaders had also criticised the Bhagwant Mann-led government over several issues, including the drug menace, rising state debt, alleged governance failures and unfulfilled promises.Speaking to the media in Chandigarh on Sunday, Jouramajra questioned the government's handling of the drug problem and raised the cases of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was killed in Mansa, and Dalit man Gulzar Singh, who died by suicide in Sangrur.He also criticised the government over its failure to fulfil the promise of providing minimum support price for crops and alleged a shortage of teachers in government schools.Pathanmajra, meanwhile, accused AAP leaders from Delhi of controlling the Punjab government and claimed that state ministers lacked the authority to independently approve even a single file.AAP leaders accuse BJP of inducting 'rejected' politiciansReacting to the resignations, Punjab AAP president Aman Arora accused the BJP of attempting to induct leaders who had left or been expelled from other parties.AAP chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal also criticised the BJP, describing it as a 'kabaad di dukaan' (scrap shop) for collecting rejected political faces.Arora said the party had taken action against its own leaders whenever they allegedly acted against Punjab's interests.Meanwhile, speculation has emerged that both legislators could join the BJP. articles.title: Stray dog reportedly bites off child's ear: Safety precautions parents should take to protect children from dog attacks while playing outdoors and moving around residential areas
articles.summary: A CCTV clip from Ambala City in Haryana has left many parents shaken.
articles.body: A CCTV clip from Ambala City in Haryana has left many parents shaken. According to a post shared on X by NCIB, the footage shows a stray dog suddenly attacking a young child who was playing outside his home. The video showcases the child was left in critical condition and that the dog reportedly bit off his ear. The post asks a question many families are now asking: if children are not safe even in their own neighbourhoods, who is responsible for their safety? For parents, the incident is a painful reminder of how quickly an ordinary moment outside the house can turn dangerous. Here is what it raises for families and what can help.A familiar scene and a frightening reminderA child playing outside the gate, in the lane or in front of the house is one of the most ordinary sights in an Indian neighbourhood. Parents feel reassured by familiar streets and nearby neighbours. The video, as described in the post, shows how that sense of safety can break in seconds. The attack apparently came without warning, which is what makes such incidents so alarming.Who is responsible?The post argues that parents must remain vigilant and that authorities must take effective measures to prevent such attacks. Both points deserve to be heard together. Parents can reduce risk, but no family can guard a child every second, and no parent should be blamed for an attack. Local bodies are responsible for managing stray animals, including sterilisation, vaccination and shelters, while residents’ associations can raise concerns and report aggressive dogs. Safety works best as a shared effort between families, neighbours and authorities.Simple steps parents can takeSupervise young children outdoors. Keep an adult within sight and reach when small children play outside, especially at dusk, early morning and in lanes where stray dogs roam.Know your neighbourhood. Notice which areas have dog packs, where dogs shelter or are fed, and avoid those spots for play. Report aggressive or sick animals to the local municipal body.Choose safer play areas. Fenced courtyards, parks with gates or playgrounds with a clear view of the surroundings are better than open streets.Be careful around feeding spots. Dogs can be more defensive near food, puppies or sleeping areas, so ask children to keep away.What to teach childrenChildren should know that they must never approach, tease, chase or pet an unfamiliar dog, and never disturb a dog that is eating, sleeping or caring for puppies. Teach them to stay calm, stand still, avoid running and screaming, keep their hands close to their body, and slowly back away if a dog comes near. If they are bitten or frightened, they should tell an adult at once, even if the injury seems small. Role-playing these steps at home helps children remember them under stress.Here's the video:If a child is bittenHealth authorities advise washing the wound immediately and thoroughly with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and then going to a doctor or hospital without delay. Do not apply chilli, turmeric or other home remedies, and do not bandage the wound tightly. Because rabies is a serious risk after any dog bite, a doctor will advise on vaccination and, if needed, other treatment, so please do not delay or skip it, even if the dog looked healthy. Serious bleeding or injury needs emergency care first.Looking aheadIncidents like this often trigger anger, fear and calls for action. For parents, the most helpful response is practical: stay alert, teach children simple safety rules and raise concerns with local authorities. For authorities, the question raised in the post remains. Neighbourhoods should be safe places for children to play.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
